plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful deciduous tree that produces clouds of delicate, fragrant blossoms before its leaves emerge. It is the most celebrated ornamental cherry in Japan and is widely planted in parks and along rivers and streets in temperate cities worldwide.
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), Korea, and temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: The famous cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom typically falls near the end of March or early April.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A hardy bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler outer petals. It grows in woodlands and meadows and is the parent of countless cultivated daffodil varieties found in spring gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to mid-spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Belgium; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of the daffodil contain lycorine and other toxic alkaloids, which is why deer and rodents generally leave the bulbs and flowers alone.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A spectacular tree from the Himalayas that bears huge, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches in early spring. Blooms can reach 25 cm across and make a dramatic display in mild-climate gardens and in the wild forests of the eastern Himalayas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, Sikkim, Yunnan); cultivated in mild gardens in the UK, New Zealand, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Magnolia campbellii may take 20 to 30 years from seed to flower for the first time, so gardeners need real patience.
